source.title: Combining Self-Supervised and Supervised Learning with Noisy Labels
source.authors: Yong-Qi Zhang; Hui Zhang; Quanming Yao; Jun Wan

record.file_problem: Full text supplied; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: The paper uses claims about robustness to noisy labels and self-supervised representations to build CS3 NL, then reports how that method performs. It does not test the listed versions about memorizing random labels, width, architecture comparisons, optimizers, batch size, dropout, sharpness, or removing memorized examples.
record.gate_note: Table 1 and Table 2 results for CS3 NL and other methods are comparisons of the paper's proposed method and baselines; baseline results are copied from prior work. Table 3 reports ablations of the proposed method, including a Standard baseline. The reported measure is validation accuracy under label noise, not the train–test gap or natural-label generalization described in the versions. Table 3 is recorded as an adjacent finding with versions ["none"].
record.test_reason: The study uses noisy-label memorization as motivation for a robust training method and reports that method's accuracy and ablations. It does not measure random-label fitting alongside natural-label generalization or test any other listed version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that noisy labels damage representation learning more than classifier learning, that classifiers can remain robust given good representations, and that their combined self-supervised and supervised framework improves noisy-label classification.
record.recipe_differences: The study proposes a new training framework combining BYOL self-supervised learning, classifier training on noisy labels, label cleaning, and representation alignment; it does not reproduce the claim versions' methods.
record.method_sensitivity: The ablations report different validation accuracies when the classifier uses the online backbone, when stop-gradient is removed, when label cleaning is removed, or when the representation-alignment loss is removed; the stop-gradient ablation has a larger accuracy drop at higher noise levels.

fits_no_version.finding: On CIFAR-10 with ResNet34, Standard validation accuracy is 96.8%, 81.3%, and 62.9% at 0%, 40%, and 80% symmetric noise; CS3 NL reaches 96.9%, 94.6%, and 88.1%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Combining self-supervised representations, supervised classifier training, and label cleaning improves robustness to partial label corruption.

fits_no_version.finding: Removing stop-gradient reduces accuracy by 1.1, 3.2, and 7.4 percentage points as noise increases; the other ablations also lower reported accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Protecting representations from noisy supervised gradients contributes to CS3 NL's robustness.

record.problems: The Table 3 ablation study reports validation accuracy but no uncertainty estimates. The paper does not report training error alongside test/validation error, so it does not measure the train–test gap.
record.rows_left_out: Table 1 and Table 2 results are comparisons of the proposed method with baselines; Table 1 baselines are stated to come from cited work, and Table 2 says results of other methods are copied from cited work. They do not measure any listed claim version, so they are not included as rows.

untested.parts: Coexistence of near-perfect random-label training fit and above-chance natural-label held-out accuracy under the same architecture and recipe; chance held-out accuracy with random labels.
Test error as width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and the roles of local connectivity, sparsity, and initialization.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer performance under limited or broader tuning and recovery recipes.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout effects across data sizes, dropout strengths, augmentation, and weight-decay conditions.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, its correlation with generalization gaps, and comparison with other measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: All recorded numbers match Table 3. These method-performance and ablation rows belong under adjacent findings rather than listed-claim evidence; their accuracy differences do not warrant observed or partial states for V1–V8. Tables 1 and 2 are already declared in rows_left_out.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out accuracy on natural labels for the same architectures and recipes.
Width sweeps beyond the interpolation threshold and resulting test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image-classifier comparisons and the stated architectural conditions.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer comparisons under different tuning regimes.
Large versus small batch comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Dropout comparisons across training-set sizes, dropout levels, and weight-decay conditions.
Magnitude-aware sharpness measurements and their relationship to train–test gaps.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the resulting test-accuracy change.
